title.en: Volume 172 Biographies 122: Ling Huchu, Niu Sengru, Xiaomian, Li Shi
title.raw: 卷一百七十二 列傳第一百二十二: 令狐楚 牛僧孺 蕭俛 李石 Volume 172 Biographies 122: Ling Huchu, Niu Sengru, Xiaomian, Li Shi

sentences.zh: 令狐楚，字殼士，自言國初十八學士德棻之裔。

translations.literal: Linghu Chu, styled Qiaoshi, claimed himself a descendant of Defen, one of the Eighteen Scholars of the early dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chu, styled Qiaoshi, claimed to be descended from Defen, one of the Eighteen Scholars of the early dynasty.

sentences.zh: 祖崇亮，綿州昌明縣令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chongliang was magistrate of Changming County in Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chongliang served as magistrate of Changming County in Mian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父承簡，太原府功曹。

translations.literal: His father Chengjian was a merit clerk in the Taiyuan prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengjian served as a merit clerk in the Taiyuan prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 家世儒素。

translations.literal: His family for generations had been devoted to Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been devoted to Confucian learning for generations.

sentences.zh: 楚兒童時已學屬文，弱冠應進士，貞元七年登第。

translations.literal: Chu had already studied literary composition as a child; in his youth he took the jinshi examination and passed in the seventh year of the Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Chu had studied literary composition since childhood. In his youth he took the jinshi examination and passed in the seventh year of the Zhenyuan era.

sentences.zh: 桂管觀察使王拱愛其才，欲以禮辟召，懼楚不從，乃先聞奏而後致聘。

translations.literal: Guiguan Observation Commissioner Wang Gong admired his talent and wished to summon him with ceremony, but feared Chu would not come; he therefore first reported to the throne and then sent the invitation.
translations.idiomatic: Guiguan Observation Commissioner Wang Gong admired his talent and wished to summon him with ceremony, but feared Chu would refuse; he therefore first reported to the throne and then sent the invitation.

sentences.zh: 楚以父掾太原，有庭闈之戀，又感拱厚意，登第後徑往桂林謝拱。

translations.literal: Because Chu's father served as a clerk in Taiyuan, he felt longing for home, and moved by Gong's generous regard, after passing the examination he went straight to Guilin to thank Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father served as a clerk in Taiyuan, Chu longed to remain near home; moved by Gong's generous regard, after passing the examination he went straight to Guilin to thank him.

sentences.zh: 不預宴遊，乞歸奉養，即還太原，人皆義之。

translations.literal: He did not join banquets and excursions, but begged leave to return and support his parents, then went back to Taiyuan; all considered this righteous.
translations.idiomatic: He declined banquets and excursions, begged leave to return and care for his parents, and went back to Taiyuan; all admired his conduct.

sentences.zh: 李說、嚴綬、鄭儋相繼鎮太原，高其行義，皆辟為從事。

translations.literal: Li Shuo, Yan Shou, and Zheng Dan successively governed Taiyuan, admired his conduct and righteousness, and all recruited him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuo, Yan Shou, and Zheng Dan, who successively governed Taiyuan, admired his character and all recruited him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 自掌書記至節度判官，歷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: From chief secretary to military commission judge, he served as Attending Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from chief secretary to military commission judge and served as Attending Censor in the Palace.

sentences.zh: 楚才思俊麗。

translations.literal: Chu's literary talent was outstanding and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's literary talent was outstanding and elegant.

sentences.zh: 德宗好文，每太原奏至，能辨楚之所為，頗稱之。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong loved literature; whenever memorials arrived from Taiyuan, he could tell which were written by Chu and greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong loved literature. Whenever memorials arrived from Taiyuan, he could tell which were written by Chu and praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 鄭儋在鎮暴卒，不及處分後事，軍中喧嘩，將有急變。

translations.literal: Zheng Dan died suddenly while in command, before arrangements for later matters could be made; the army clamored and there was about to be a sudden crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Dan died suddenly while in command, before later arrangements could be made. The army clamored and a sudden crisis was imminent.

sentences.zh: 中夜十數騎持刃迫楚至軍門，諸將環之，令草遺表。

translations.literal: In the middle of the night a dozen horsemen with drawn blades forced Chu to the army gate; the generals surrounded him and ordered him to draft a final memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle of the night a dozen horsemen with drawn blades forced Chu to the army gate. The generals surrounded him and ordered him to draft a final memorial.

sentences.zh: 楚在白刃之中，搦管即成，讀示三軍，無不感泣，軍情乃安。

translations.literal: Chu, amid naked blades, took up the brush and finished at once; when it was read to the whole army, none failed to weep, and the army's mood was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Amid naked blades, Chu took up the brush and finished at once. When it was read to the whole army, all wept, and the army's mood was settled.

sentences.zh: 自是聲名益重。

translations.literal: From this his reputation grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: From this his reputation grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，以孝聞。

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he observed mourning and was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 免喪，徵拜右拾遺，改太常博士、禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: After mourning ended he was summoned as Right Reminder and changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended he was summoned as Right Reminder, then appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 母憂去官。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office.

sentences.zh: 服闋，以刑部員外郎征，轉職方員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned as Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, then transferred to Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments and made Drafter of Imperial Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned as Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, then transferred to Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments and appointed Drafter of Imperial Edicts.

sentences.zh: 楚與皇甫鎛、蕭俛同年登進士第。

translations.literal: Chu, Huangfu Bo, and Xiaomian passed the jinshi examination in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: Chu, Huangfu Bo, and Xiaomian passed the jinshi examination in the same year.

sentences.zh: 元和九年，鎛初以財賦得幸，薦俛、楚俱入翰林，充學士，遷職方郎中、中書舍人，皆居內職。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanhe, when Bo first won favor through fiscal administration, he recommended Xiaomian and Chu to enter the Hanlin Academy as Academicians; Chu was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Appointments and Palace Secretary, all holding inner-court posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanhe, when Bo first won favor through fiscal administration, he recommended Xiaomian and Chu for the Hanlin Academy as Academicians. Chu was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Appointments and Palace Secretary, all holding inner-court posts.

sentences.zh: 時用兵淮西，言事者以師久無功，宜宥賊罷兵，唯裴度與憲宗誌在殄寇。

translations.literal: At that time troops were being used in Huaixi; those who spoke on policy held that the campaign had long been unsuccessful and the rebels should be pardoned and the army withdrawn; only Pei Du and Emperor Xianzong were determined to destroy the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At that time troops were being used in Huaixi. Policy advisers held that the campaign had long been unsuccessful and the rebels should be pardoned and the army withdrawn; only Pei Du and Emperor Xianzong were determined to destroy the enemy.

sentences.zh: 十二年夏，度自宰相兼彰義軍節度、淮西招撫宣慰處置使。

translations.literal: In summer of the twelfth year, Du left the chancellorship to serve concurrently as military commissioner of Zhangyi Army and Pacification, Comfort, and Disposition Commissioner for Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of the twelfth year, Du left the chancellorship to serve concurrently as military commissioner of Zhangyi Army and Pacification, Comfort, and Disposition Commissioner for Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 宰相李逢吉與度不協，與楚相善。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Fengji was at odds with Du and was on good terms with Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Fengji was at odds with Du and was on good terms with Chu.

sentences.zh: 楚草度淮西招撫使制，不合度旨，度請改制內三數句語。

translations.literal: Chu drafted the edict appointing Du Pacification Commissioner for Huaixi, which did not accord with Du's intent; Du requested that several phrases in the edict be revised.
translations.idiomatic: Chu drafted the edict appointing Du Pacification Commissioner for Huaixi, which did not accord with Du's intent. Du requested that several phrases in the edict be revised.

sentences.zh: 憲宗方責度用兵，乃罷逢吉相任，亦罷楚內職，守中書舍人。

translations.literal: The emperor was then reproaching Du for his use of troops, and dismissed Fengji from the chancellorship and also removed Chu from his inner-court post, leaving him as Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then reproaching Du for his use of troops. He dismissed Fengji from the chancellorship and also removed Chu from his inner-court post, leaving him as Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年四月，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he went out as prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he was appointed prefect of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，皇甫鎛作相，其月以楚為河陽懷節度使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year Huangfu Bo became chancellor, and in that month Chu was made military commissioner of Heyang-Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year Huangfu Bo became chancellor, and in that month Chu was made military commissioner of Heyang-Huai.

sentences.zh: 十四年四月，裴度出鎮太原。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year Pei Du went out to govern Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year Pei Du went out to govern Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 七月，皇甫鎛薦楚入朝，自朝議郎授朝議大夫、中書侍郎、同平章事，與鎛同處臺衡，深承顧待。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Huangfu Bo recommended Chu to enter court; from Court Gentleman for Consultation he was appointed Court Gentleman for Discussion, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Associate Councilor of State, sharing the chancellorship with Bo and deeply enjoying imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Huangfu Bo recommended Chu to enter court. From Court Gentleman for Consultation he was appointed Court Gentleman for Discussion, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Associate Councilor of State, sharing the chancellorship with Bo and deeply enjoying imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，憲宗崩，詔楚為山陵使，仍撰哀冊文。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year Emperor Xianzong died; an edict appointed Chu Director of the Imperial Mausoleum and ordered him to compose the lamentation text.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year Emperor Xianzong died. An edict appointed Chu Director of the Imperial Mausoleum and ordered him to compose the lamentation text.

sentences.zh: 時天下怒皇甫鎛之奸邪。

translations.literal: At that time the whole realm was angry at Huangfu Bo's treachery and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the whole realm was angry at Huangfu Bo's treachery and wickedness.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位之四日，群臣素服，班於月華門外，宣詔貶鎛，將殺之。

translations.literal: On the fourth day after Emperor Muzong's accession, the officials in plain dress lined up outside the Moon Glory Gate; an edict was proclaimed demoting Bo, and he was about to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day after Emperor Muzong's accession, officials in plain dress lined up outside the Moon Glory Gate. An edict was proclaimed demoting Bo, and he was about to be executed.

sentences.zh: 會蕭俛作相，托中官救解，方貶崖州。

translations.literal: Xiaomian then became chancellor and, through inner-court eunuchs, pleaded for his release; he was finally demoted to Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaomian then became chancellor and, through inner-court eunuchs, pleaded for his release. Bo was finally demoted to Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 物議以楚因鎛作相而逐裴度，群情共怒。

translations.literal: Public opinion held that Chu had become chancellor through Bo and had driven out Pei Du; all were angry together.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that Chu had become chancellor through Bo and had driven out Pei Du; all were angry together.

sentences.zh: 以蕭俛之故，無敢措言。

translations.literal: Because of Xiaomian, none dared speak out.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Xiaomian, none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，山陵畢，會有告楚親吏贓汙事發，出為宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year, when the mausoleum work was finished, there came a report that Chu's close clerks had committed corruption; he was sent out as Observation Commissioner of Xuanchen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year, when the mausoleum work was finished, a report emerged that Chu's close clerks had committed corruption. He was sent out as Observation Commissioner of Xuanchen.

sentences.zh: 楚充奉山陵時，親吏韋正牧、奉天令于翬、翰林陰陽官等同隱官錢，不給工徒價錢，移為羨餘十五萬貫上獻。

translations.literal: While Chu was supervising the mausoleum, his close clerks Wei Zhengmu, Fengtian magistrate Yu Hui, and Hanlin Academy yin-yang officials together concealed official funds, failed to pay laborers, and transferred the surplus of 150,000 strings of cash upward as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: While Chu was supervising the mausoleum, his close clerks Wei Zhengmu, Fengtian magistrate Yu Hui, and Hanlin Academy yin-yang officials together concealed official funds, failed to pay laborers, and transferred a surplus of 150,000 strings of cash upward as tribute.

sentences.zh: 怨訴盈路，正牧等下獄伏罪，皆誅。

translations.literal: Complaints filled the roads; Zhengmu and the others were imprisoned, convicted, and all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Complaints filled the roads. Zhengmu and the others were imprisoned, convicted, and all executed.

sentences.zh: 楚再貶衡州刺史。

translations.literal: Chu was demoted again to prefect of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chu was demoted again to prefect of Heng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時元稹初得幸，為學士，素惡楚與鎛膠固希寵，稹草楚衡州制，略曰：「楚早以文藝，得踐班資，憲宗念才，擢居禁近。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zhen had just won favor and was an Academician; he had long hated Chu and Bo for clinging together in hope of favor. Zhen drafted Chu's Heng Prefecture appointment edict, which in summary said: "Chu early won office rank through literary accomplishment; Emperor Xianzong, mindful of his talent, promoted him to close attendance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zhen had just won favor and was an Academician. He had long hated Chu and Bo for clinging together in hope of favor. Zhen drafted Chu's Heng Prefecture appointment edict, which in summary said: "Chu early won office rank through literary accomplishment. Emperor Xianzong, mindful of his talent, promoted him to close attendance.

sentences.zh: 異端斯害，獨見不明，密隳討伐之謀，潛附奸邪之黨。

translations.literal: Heterodox influences harmed him; he alone lacked clear judgment, secretly undermined plans for punitive campaigns, and secretly attached himself to wicked and treacherous factions.
translations.idiomatic: Heterodox influences harmed him. He alone lacked clear judgment, secretly undermined plans for punitive campaigns, and secretly attached himself to wicked and treacherous factions.

sentences.zh: 因緣得地，進取多門，遂忝臺階，實妨賢路。」

translations.literal: By connections he gained position, advanced through many doors, then disgraced the steps of the terrace, and truly obstructed the path of the worthy."
translations.idiomatic: By connections he gained position and advanced through many doors, then disgraced the steps of the terrace and truly obstructed the path of the worthy."

sentences.zh: 楚深恨稹。

translations.literal: Chu deeply resented Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Chu deeply resented Zhen.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年四月，量移郢州刺史，遷太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Changqing he was transferred to prefect of E Prefecture, then appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and assigned to the Eastern Capital as titular official.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Changqing he was transferred to prefect of E Prefecture, then appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and assigned to the Eastern Capital as titular official.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月，授陜州大都督府長史、兼御史大夫、陜虢觀察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Prefecture of Shan, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and Observation Commissioner of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Prefecture of Shan, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and Observation Commissioner of Shan-Guo.

sentences.zh: 制下旬日，諫官論奏，言楚所犯非輕，未合居廉察之任。

translations.literal: Ten days after the edict was issued, remonstrating officials submitted memorials saying Chu's offenses were not light and he was unfit for a surveillance and investigation post.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days after the edict was issued, remonstrating officials submitted memorials saying Chu's offenses were not light and he was unfit for a surveillance and investigation post.

sentences.zh: 上知之，遽令追制。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of it and hastily ordered the edict recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of it and hastily ordered the edict recalled.

sentences.zh: 時楚已至陜州，視事一日矣。

translations.literal: By then Chu had already reached Shan Prefecture and had administered affairs for one day.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chu had already reached Shan Prefecture and had administered affairs for one day.

sentences.zh: 復授賓客，歸東都。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Grand Mentor and returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Grand Mentor and returned to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 時年逢吉作相，極力援楚，以李紳在禁密沮之，未能擅柄。

translations.literal: At that time Fengji was chancellor and strongly supported Chu, but Li Shen in the inner court obstructed him and he could not monopolize power.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fengji was chancellor and strongly supported Chu, but Li Shen in the inner court obstructed him and he could not monopolize power.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位，逢吉逐李紳，尋用楚為河南尹、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong acceded, Fengji drove out Li Shen and soon appointed Chu Metropolitan Governor of Henan and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong acceded, Fengji drove out Li Shen and soon appointed Chu Metropolitan Governor of Henan and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，檢校禮部尚書、汴州刺史、宣武軍節度、汴宋亳觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year he was made Acting Minister of Rites, prefect of Bian, military commissioner of Xuanwu Army, and observation commissioner of Bian-Song-Bo.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year he was made Acting Minister of Rites, prefect of Bian, military commissioner of Xuanwu Army, and observation commissioner of Bian-Song-Bo.

sentences.zh: 汴軍素驕，累逐主帥；

translations.literal: The Bian army had long been arrogant and repeatedly drove out their commanders;
translations.idiomatic: The Bian army had long been arrogant and repeatedly drove out their commanders;

sentences.zh: 前後韓弘兄弟，率以峻法繩之，人皆偷生，未能革誌。

translations.literal: the former commanders, the brothers Han Hong, generally restrained them with harsh law; the men merely eked out existence and their will could not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: the former commanders, the brothers Han Hong, generally restrained them with harsh law. The men merely eked out existence and their will could not be changed.

sentences.zh: 楚長於撫理，前鎮河陽，代烏重胤移鎮滄州，以河陽軍三千人為牙卒，卒咸不願從，中路叛歸，又不敢歸州，聚於境上。

translations.literal: Chu excelled at soothing administration. When he had earlier governed Heyang, Wu Chongyin was transferred from Heyang to govern Cang Prefecture; three thousand Heyang troops were made his personal guard, and the soldiers were unwilling to follow; midway they rebelled and returned, yet dared not return to the prefecture and gathered on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Chu excelled at soothing administration. When he had earlier governed Heyang, Wu Chongyin was transferred from Heyang to govern Cang Prefecture. Three thousand Heyang troops were made his personal guard, but the soldiers were unwilling to follow. Midway they rebelled and returned, yet dared not return to the prefecture and gathered on the border.

sentences.zh: 楚初赴任，聞之，乃疾驅赴懷州，潰卒亦至，楚單騎喻之，咸令橐弓解甲，用為前驅，卒不敢亂。

translations.literal: When Chu first took up his post and heard of it, he galloped swiftly to Huai Prefecture; the scattered soldiers also arrived. Chu went alone on horseback to instruct them, ordered them all to sheath bows and lay aside armor, and used them as vanguard; the soldiers dared not cause disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu first took up his post and heard of it, he galloped swiftly to Huai Prefecture. The scattered soldiers also arrived. Chu went alone on horseback to instruct them, ordered them all to sheath bows and lay aside armor, and used them as vanguard. The soldiers dared not cause disorder.

sentences.zh: 及蒞汴州，解其酷法，以仁惠為治，去其太甚，軍民咸悅，翕然從化，後竟為善地。

translations.literal: When he arrived at Bian Prefecture he abolished harsh laws and governed with benevolence and kindness, removing excesses; soldiers and people alike were pleased, united in submission, and it later became a good region.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived at Bian Prefecture he abolished harsh laws and governed with benevolence and kindness, removing excesses. Soldiers and people alike were pleased, united in submission, and it later became a good region.

sentences.zh: 汴帥前例，始至率以錢二百萬實其私藏，楚獨不取，以其羨財治廨舍數百間。

translations.literal: By former precedent, when a Bian commander first arrived he generally deposited two million cash in his private store; Chu alone did not take it and used the surplus funds to repair several hundred government buildings.
translations.idiomatic: By former precedent, when a Bian commander first arrived he generally deposited two million cash in his private store. Chu alone did not take it and used the surplus funds to repair several hundred government buildings.

sentences.zh: 太和二年九月，徵為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Taihe he was summoned as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Taihe he was summoned as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，檢校兵部尚書、東都留守、東畿汝都防禦使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year he was made Acting Minister of War, Eastern Capital Garrison Commander, and Defense Commissioner of the Eastern Capital and Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year he was made Acting Minister of War, Eastern Capital Garrison Commander, and Defense Commissioner of the Eastern Capital and Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，進位檢校右僕射、鄆州刺史、天平軍節度、鄆曹濮觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year he was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State, prefect of Yan, military commissioner of Tianping Army, and observation commissioner of Yan-Cao-Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year he was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State, prefect of Yan, military commissioner of Tianping Army, and observation commissioner of Yan-Cao-Pu.

sentences.zh: 奏故東平縣為天平縣。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the former Dongping County be made Tianping County.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the former Dongping County be made Tianping County.

sentences.zh: 屬歲旱儉，人至相食，楚均富贍貧，而無流亡者。

translations.literal: When drought and famine struck that year and people came to eat one another, Chu equalized the rich to support the poor and there were no displaced persons.
translations.idiomatic: When drought and famine struck that year and people came to eat one another, Chu equalized the rich to support the poor and there were no displaced persons.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，改太原尹、北都留守、河東節度等使。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year he was changed to Metropolitan Governor of Taiyuan, Northern Capital Garrison Commander, and military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year he was changed to Metropolitan Governor of Taiyuan, Northern Capital Garrison Commander, and military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 楚久在并州，練其風俗，因人所利而利之，雖屬歲旱，人無轉徙。

translations.literal: Chu had long been in Bingzhou and was versed in its customs; he benefited people through what they themselves found beneficial, and even in years of drought the people did not migrate.
translations.idiomatic: Chu had long been in Bingzhou and was versed in its customs. He benefited people through what they themselves found beneficial, and even in years of drought the people did not migrate.

sentences.zh: 楚始自書生，隨計成名，皆在太原，實如故裏。

translations.literal: Chu had begun as a scholar; through the examination he achieved fame, and all was in Taiyuan—it was truly like his old home.
translations.idiomatic: Chu had begun as a scholar. Through the examination he achieved fame, and all was in Taiyuan—it was truly like his old home.

sentences.zh: 及是垂旄作鎮，邑老歡迎。

translations.literal: When he now governed with white hair hanging down, the elders of the district welcomed him joyfully.
translations.idiomatic: When he now governed with white hair hanging down, the elders of the district welcomed him joyfully.

sentences.zh: 楚綏撫有方，軍民胥悅。

translations.literal: Chu soothed and governed with proper method; soldiers and people alike were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Chu soothed and governed with proper method; soldiers and people alike were pleased.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，入為吏部尚書，仍檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year he entered court as Minister of Personnel, still Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year he entered court as Minister of Personnel, still Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State.

sentences.zh: 故事，檢校高官者，便從其班。

translations.literal: By precedent, those holding acting high offices followed their acting rank in court order.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, those holding acting high offices followed their acting rank in court order.

sentences.zh: 楚以正官三品不宜從二品之列，請從本班，優詔嘉之。

translations.literal: Chu held that a regular third-rank official should not stand in second-rank order and requested to stand in his regular rank; an edict of praise approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Chu held that a regular third-rank official should not stand in second-rank order and requested to stand in his regular rank. An edict of praise approved this.

sentences.zh: 九年六月，轉太常卿。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year he was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year he was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十月，守尚書左僕射，進封彭陽郡開國公。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State and was advanced to Duke of Pengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State and was advanced to Duke of Pengyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，李訓兆亂，京師大擾。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Li Xun plotted rebellion and the capital was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Li Xun plotted rebellion and the capital was greatly disturbed.

sentences.zh: 訓亂之夜，文宗召右僕射鄭覃與楚宿於禁中，商量制敕，上皆欲用為宰相。

translations.literal: On the night of Xun's rebellion, Emperor Wenzong summoned Right Vice Director Zheng Tan and Chu to stay in the inner palace to discuss edicts; the emperor wished to use both as chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of Xun's rebellion, Emperor Wenzong summoned Right Vice Director Zheng Tan and Chu to stay in the inner palace to discuss edicts. The emperor wished to use both as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 楚以王涯、賈餗冤死，敘其罪狀浮泛，仇士良等不悅，故輔弼之命移於李石。

translations.literal: Chu held that Wang Ya and Jia Su had died unjustly and that the account of their crimes was vague and superficial; Qiu Shiliang and others were displeased, and so the appointment to the chancellorship shifted to Li Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Chu held that Wang Ya and Jia Su had died unjustly and that the account of their crimes was vague and superficial. Qiu Shiliang and others were displeased, and so the appointment to the chancellorship shifted to Li Shi.

sentences.zh: 乃以本官領鹽鐵轉運等使。

translations.literal: He then held his regular office and concurrently headed the Salt and Iron Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He then held his regular office and concurrently headed the Salt and Iron Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 先是，鄭註上封置榷茶使額，鹽鐵使兼領之，楚奏罷之，曰：

translations.literal: Earlier, Zheng Zhu had submitted a sealed memorial to establish a tea monopoly commissioner quota, which the salt commissioner concurrently held; Chu memorialized to abolish it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zheng Zhu had submitted a sealed memorial to establish a tea monopoly commissioner quota, which the salt commissioner concurrently held. Chu memorialized to abolish it, saying:

sentences.zh: 前月二十一日，內殿奏對之次，鄭覃與臣同陳論訖。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of last month, during an audience in the inner hall, Zheng Tan and I together finished presenting our views.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day of last month, during an audience in the inner hall, Zheng Tan and I together finished presenting our views.

sentences.zh: 伏望聖慈早賜處分，一依舊法，不用新條。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Sacred Kindness will soon grant disposition and follow the old law entirely, not using the new regulations.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Sacred Kindness will soon grant disposition and follow the old law entirely, not using the new regulations.

sentences.zh: 唯納榷之時，須節級加價，商人轉賣，必校稍貴，即是錢出萬國，利歸有司。

translations.literal: Only when collecting the monopoly levy should prices be raised by stages; when merchants resell, prices must be somewhat higher—thus money comes from all lands and profit returns to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Only when collecting the monopoly levy should prices be raised by stages. When merchants resell, prices must be somewhat higher—thus money comes from all lands and profit returns to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 既不害茶商，又不擾茶戶，上以彰陛下愛人之德，下以竭微臣憂國之心。

translations.literal: This neither harms tea merchants nor disturbs tea households; above it manifests Your Majesty's virtue of loving the people, below it exhausts this humble minister's heart of concern for the state.
translations.idiomatic: This neither harms tea merchants nor disturbs tea households. Above it manifests Your Majesty's virtue of loving the people; below it exhausts this humble minister's heart of concern for the state.

sentences.zh: 遠近傳聞，必當感悅。

translations.literal: When the report spreads far and near, all will surely be moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the report spreads far and near, all will surely be moved and pleased.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 先是，元和十年，出內庫弓箭陌刀賜左右街使，充宰相入朝以為翼衛，及建福門而止。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the tenth year of Yuanhe, bows, arrows, and broadswords from the inner storehouse were issued to the left and right street commissioners; chancellors entering court used them as escort guards, stopping at the Jianfu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the tenth year of Yuanhe, bows, arrows, and broadswords from the inner storehouse were issued to the left and right street commissioners. Chancellors entering court used them as escort guards, stopping at the Jianfu Gate.

sentences.zh: 至是，因訓、註之亂，悉罷之。

translations.literal: Now, because of the rebellion of Xun and Zhu, all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Now, because of the rebellion of Xun and Zhu, all were abolished.

sentences.zh: 楚又奏：「諸道新授方鎮節度使等，具帑抹，帶器仗，就尚書省兵部參辭。

translations.literal: Chu also memorialized: "Newly appointed military commissioners of the various circuits and the like should bring traveling funds and weapons and present themselves for audience at the Ministry of War in the Department of State.
translations.idiomatic: Chu also memorialized: "Newly appointed military commissioners of the various circuits and the like should bring traveling funds and weapons and present themselves for audience at the Ministry of War in the Department of State.

sentences.zh: 伏以軍國異容，古今定制，若不由舊，斯為改常。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that military and civil attire differ; ancient and modern regulations are fixed; if the old way is not followed, this is to change what is constant.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that military and civil attire differ and ancient and modern regulations are fixed. If the old way is not followed, this is to change what is constant.

sentences.zh: 未聞省閣之門，忽內弓刀之器。

translations.literal: I have never heard of bow-and-blade weapons suddenly inside the gates of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: I have never heard of bow-and-blade weapons suddenly inside the gates of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鄭註外蒙恩寵，內蓄兇狂，首創奸謀，將興亂兆。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu outwardly received imperial favor yet inwardly harbored fierce wickedness; he first devised treacherous plots and was about to raise the omen of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu outwardly received imperial favor yet inwardly harbored fierce wickedness. He first devised treacherous plots and was about to raise the omen of disorder.

sentences.zh: 致王璠、郭行余之輩，敢驅將吏，直詣闕庭。

translations.literal: He caused men like Wang Fan and Guo Xingyu to dare drive generals and clerks straight to the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: He caused men like Wang Fan and Guo Xingyu to dare drive generals and clerks straight to the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 震驚乘輿，騷動京國，血濺朝路，屍僵禁街。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage was shaken, the capital disturbed; blood splashed on the road to court, corpses lay stiff in the forbidden streets.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage was shaken and the capital disturbed. Blood splashed on the road to court and corpses lay stiff in the forbidden streets.

sentences.zh: 史冊所書，人神共憤，既往不咎，其源尚開。

translations.literal: What histories record, men and spirits alike resent; though the past is not blamed, the source remains open.
translations.idiomatic: What histories record, men and spirits alike resent. Though the past is not blamed, the source remains open.

sentences.zh: 前件事宜，伏乞速令停罷，如須參謝，即具公服。」

translations.literal: Regarding the former matter, I humbly beg that it be swiftly ordered stopped; if audience is required, let them wear only official robes."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding the former matter, I humbly beg that it be swiftly ordered stopped. If audience is required, let them wear only official robes."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又奏請罷修曲江亭絹一萬三千七百匹，回修尚書省，從之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting abolition of the 13,700 bolts of silk for repairing Qujiang Pavilion and their reallocation to repair the Department of State; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized requesting abolition of the 13,700 bolts of silk for repairing Qujiang Pavilion and their reallocation to repair the Department of State. The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 開成元年上巳，賜百僚曲江亭宴。

translations.literal: On the third day of the third month in the first year of Kaicheng, the emperor bestowed a banquet at Qujiang Pavilion on the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the third month in the first year of Kaicheng, the emperor bestowed a banquet at Qujiang Pavilion on the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 楚以新誅大臣，不宜賞宴，獨稱疾不赴，論者美之。

translations.literal: Chu held that since great ministers had just been executed, it was improper to reward them with a banquet; he alone pleaded illness and did not attend, and commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Chu held that since great ministers had just been executed, it was improper to reward them with a banquet. He alone pleaded illness and did not attend, and commentators praised him.

sentences.zh: 以權在內官，累上疏乞解使務。

translations.literal: Because power lay with inner-court eunuchs, he repeatedly submitted memorials begging to be relieved of commission duties.
translations.idiomatic: Because power lay with inner-court eunuchs, he repeatedly submitted memorials begging to be relieved of commission duties.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，檢校左僕射、興元尹，充山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year he was made Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State and Metropolitan Governor of Xingyuan, military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of that year he was made Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State and Metropolitan Governor of Xingyuan, military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月，卒於鎮，年七十二，冊贈司空，謚曰文。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year he died in his post at age seventy-two; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year he died in his post at age seventy-two. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 楚風儀嚴重，若不可犯；

translations.literal: Chu's bearing was stern and grave, as if he could not be violated;
translations.idiomatic: Chu's bearing was stern and grave, as if he could not be violated;

sentences.zh: 然寬厚有禮，門無雜賓。

translations.literal: yet he was generous and courteous, and no improper guests entered his gate.
translations.idiomatic: yet he was generous and courteous, and no improper guests entered his gate.

sentences.zh: 嘗與從事宴語方酣，有非類偶至，立命徹席，毅然色變。

translations.literal: Once while drinking and conversing with aides he was in high spirits; when someone unfitting arrived by chance, he immediately ordered the feast withdrawn and his expression turned stern.
translations.idiomatic: Once while drinking and conversing with aides he was in high spirits. When someone unfitting arrived by chance, he immediately ordered the feast withdrawn and his expression turned stern.

sentences.zh: 累居重任，貞操如初。

translations.literal: Though he repeatedly held heavy responsibility, his integrity remained as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Though he repeatedly held heavy responsibility, his integrity remained as at first.

sentences.zh: 未終前三日，猶吟詠自若。

translations.literal: Three days before his end he still chanted and composed as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before his end he still chanted and composed as usual.

sentences.zh: 疾甚，諸子進藥，未賞入口，曰：「修短之期，分以定矣，何須此物？」

translations.literal: When his illness was severe his sons brought medicine; before it entered his mouth he said: "The term of life long or short is already fixed by fate—why need this thing?"
translations.idiomatic: When his illness was severe his sons brought medicine. Before it entered his mouth he said: "The term of life long or short is already fixed by fate—why need this thing?"

sentences.zh: 前一日，召從事李商隱曰：「吾氣魄已殫，情思俱盡，然所懷未已，強欲自寫聞天，恐辭語乖舛，子當助我成之。」

translations.literal: The day before, he summoned his aide Li Shangyin and said: "My vital breath is already exhausted and my feelings and thoughts are all spent; yet what I still carry has not ended. I force myself to write and inform Heaven, but fear my words may be mistaken—you must help me complete it."
translations.idiomatic: The day before, he summoned his aide Li Shangyin and said: "My vital breath is already exhausted and my feelings and thoughts are all spent, yet what I still carry has not ended. I force myself to write and inform Heaven, but fear my words may be mistaken—you must help me complete it."

sentences.zh: 即秉筆自書曰：

translations.literal: He then took up the brush and wrote himself:
translations.idiomatic: He then took up the brush and wrote himself:

sentences.zh: 書訖，謂其子緒、綯曰：「吾生無益於人，勿請謚號。

translations.literal: When the writing was finished he told his sons Xu and Tao: "In life I was of no benefit to others—do not request a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When the writing was finished he told his sons Xu and Tao: "In life I was of no benefit to others—do not request a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 葬日，勿請鼓吹，唯以布車一乘，余勿加飾。

translations.literal: On the day of burial do not request ceremonial music; use only one cloth carriage and add no further ornament.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial do not request ceremonial music. Use only one cloth carriage and add no further ornament.

sentences.zh: 銘誌但誌宗門，秉筆者無擇高位。」

translations.literal: The inscription should record only the clan; let the writer not be chosen for high rank."
translations.idiomatic: The inscription should record only the clan. Let the writer not be chosen for high rank."

sentences.zh: 當歿之夕，有大星隕於寢室之上，其光燭廷。

translations.literal: On the night of his death a great star fell above his sleeping chamber and its light illuminated the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of his death a great star fell above his sleeping chamber and its light illuminated the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 楚端坐與家人告訣，言已而終。

translations.literal: Chu sat upright and took leave of his family; when he finished speaking he died.
translations.idiomatic: Chu sat upright and took leave of his family. When he finished speaking he died.

sentences.zh: 嗣子奉行遺旨。

translations.literal: His heir carried out his final instructions.
translations.idiomatic: His heir carried out his final instructions.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「生為名臣，歿有理命。

translations.literal: An edict said: "In life he was a famed minister; in death he had a rational fate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "In life he was a famed minister; in death he had a rational fate.

sentences.zh: 終始之分，可謂兩全。

translations.literal: The division of beginning and end may be called fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: The division of beginning and end may be called fully complete.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿哀榮之末節，難違往意；

translations.literal: The final rites of escort and glory are minor matters and hard to violate his former intent;
translations.idiomatic: The final rites of escort and glory are minor matters and hard to violate his former intent;

sentences.zh: 誄謚國家之大典，須守彜章。

translations.literal: eulogy and posthumous title are great state ceremonies and must observe constant rules.
translations.idiomatic: eulogy and posthumous title are great state ceremonies and must observe constant rules.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿宜停，易名須準舊例。」

translations.literal: The escort guard should stop; changing the name must follow former precedent."
translations.idiomatic: The escort guard should stop; changing the name must follow former precedent."

sentences.zh: 後綯貴，累贈至太尉。

translations.literal: Later when Tao became eminent, he was repeatedly posthumously advanced to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Tao became eminent, he was repeatedly posthumously advanced to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 有文集一百卷，行於時。

translations.literal: He had a collected works of one hundred scrolls circulating in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collected works of one hundred scrolls circulating in his time.

sentences.zh: 所撰《憲宗哀冊文》，辭情典郁，為文士所重。

translations.literal: The Lamentation Text for Emperor Xianzong that he composed was rich and solemn in literary feeling and was valued by writers.
translations.idiomatic: The Lamentation Text for Emperor Xianzong that he composed was rich and solemn in literary feeling and was valued by writers.

sentences.zh: 楚弟定，字履常。

translations.literal: Chu's younger brother Ding, styled Luchang.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's younger brother Ding, styled Luchang.

sentences.zh: 元和十一年進士及第，累辟使府。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly recruited to commissioner staffs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly recruited to commissioner staffs.

sentences.zh: 太和九年，累遷至職方員外郎、弘文館直學士、檢校右散騎常侍、桂州刺史、桂管都防禦觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments, Academician of the Hongwen Hall, Acting Right Regular Cavalryman, prefect of Gui, and defense and observation commissioner of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taihe he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments, Academician of the Hongwen Hall, Acting Right Regular Cavalryman, prefect of Gui, and defense and observation commissioner of Gui.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 緒以廕授官，歷隨、壽、汝三郡刺史。

translations.literal: Xu received office by hereditary privilege and served successively as prefect of Sui, Shou, and Ru prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Xu received office by hereditary privilege and served successively as prefect of Sui, Shou, and Ru prefectures.

sentences.zh: 在汝州日，有能政，郡人請立碑頌德。

translations.literal: While in Ru Prefecture he had able administration, and the people of the prefecture requested an inscribed stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: While in Ru Prefecture he had able administration, and the people of the prefecture requested an inscribed stele praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 緒以弟襜在輔弼，上言曰：「臣先父元和中特承恩顧，弟綯官不因人，出自宸衷。

translations.literal: Because his younger brother Can was in the chancellorship, Xu submitted a memorial saying: "My late father in the Yuanhe era specially received imperial favor; my younger brother Tao's office did not come through others but issued from the imperial heart.
translations.idiomatic: Because his younger brother Can was in the chancellorship, Xu submitted a memorial saying: "My late father in the Yuanhe era specially received imperial favor. My younger brother Tao's office did not come through others but issued from the imperial heart.

sentences.zh: 臣伏睹詔書，以臣刺汝州日，粗立政勞，吏民求立碑頌，尋乞追罷。

translations.literal: Your servant has seen the edict that because I governed Ru Prefecture and roughly established administrative merit, officials and people sought to erect a stele of praise; I beg that this be recalled and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has seen the edict that because I governed Ru Prefecture and roughly established administrative merit, officials and people sought to erect a stele of praise. I beg that this be recalled and stopped.

sentences.zh: 臣任隨州日，郡人乞留，得上下考。

translations.literal: When I governed Sui Prefecture the people begged me to remain and I received top and bottom ratings in assessment.
translations.idiomatic: When I governed Sui Prefecture the people begged me to remain and I received top and bottom ratings in assessment.

sentences.zh: 及轉河南少尹，加金紫。

translations.literal: When I was transferred to Vice Governor of Henan I was given gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: When I was transferred to Vice Governor of Henan I was given gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 此名已聞於日下，不必更立碑頌，乞賜寢停。」

translations.literal: This fame is already known below the sun; there is no need to erect another stele of praise. I beg that this be granted and stopped."
translations.idiomatic: This fame is already known below the sun; there is no need to erect another stele of praise. I beg that this be granted and stopped."

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘉其意，從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong approved his intent and consented.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong approved his intent and consented.

sentences.zh: 綯字子直。

translations.literal: Tao, styled Zizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Tao, styled Zizhi.

sentences.zh: 太和四年登進士第，釋褐弘文館校書郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he passed the jinshi examination and on leaving office became Proofreader of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe he passed the jinshi examination and on leaving office became Proofreader of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 開成初為左拾遺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng he became Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaicheng he became Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 二年，丁父喪。

translations.literal: In the second year he observed mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he observed mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授本官，尋改左補闕、史館修撰，累遷庫部、戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed to his former office, soon changed to Left Supplementation Official and Compiler of the History Institute, and repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Treasuries and Revenue ministries.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed to his former office, soon changed to Left Supplementation Official and Compiler of the History Institute, and repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Treasuries and Revenue ministries.

sentences.zh: 會昌五年，出為湖州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huichang he went out as prefect of Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Huichang he went out as prefect of Hu.

sentences.zh: 大中二年，召拜考功郎中，尋知制誥。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong he was summoned as Director in the Bureau of Evaluations and soon made Drafter of Imperial Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dazhong he was summoned as Director in the Bureau of Evaluations and soon made Drafter of Imperial Edicts.

sentences.zh: 其年，召入充翰林學士。

translations.literal: In that year he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In that year he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜中書舍人，襲封彭陽男，食邑三百戶，尋拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Palace Secretary, inherited the title Baron of Pengyang with a fief of three hundred households, and soon made Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Palace Secretary, inherited the title Baron of Pengyang with a fief of three hundred households, and soon made Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 四年，轉戶部侍郎，判本司事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and directed the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and directed the ministry's affairs.

sentences.zh: 其年，改兵部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In that year he was changed to Vice Minister of War and Associate Councilor of State through the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In that year he was changed to Vice Minister of War and Associate Councilor of State through the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 綯以舊事帶尚書省官，合先省上。

translations.literal: By former precedent, when one concurrently held a Ministry of State office one should first report to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: By former precedent, when one concurrently held a Ministry of State office one should first report to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 上日同列集於少府監。

translations.literal: On the day of assumption his colleagues gathered at the Office of the Director of Palace Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of assumption his colleagues gathered at the Office of the Director of Palace Supplies.

sentences.zh: 時白敏中、崔龜從曾為太常博士，至相位，欲榮其舊署，乃改集於太常禮院，龜從手筆誌其事於壁。

translations.literal: At that time Bai Minzhong and Cui Guicong had once been Directors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; when they reached the chancellorship they wished to honor their former office and changed the gathering to the Ceremonial Court of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Guicong personally wrote and recorded the matter on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Bai Minzhong and Cui Guicong had once been Directors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. When they reached the chancellorship they wished to honor their former office and changed the gathering to the Ceremonial Court of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Guicong personally wrote and recorded the matter on the wall.

sentences.zh: 綯輔政十年，累官至吏部尚書、右僕射、涼國公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Tao assisted in government for ten years and was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Personnel, Right Vice Director of the Department of State, and Duke of Liang with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Tao assisted in government for ten years and was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Personnel, Right Vice Director of the Department of State, and Duke of Liang with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 十三年，罷相，檢校司空、同中書門下平章事、河中尹、河中晉絳等節度使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was dismissed from the chancellorship and made Acting Minister of Works, Associate Councilor of State, Metropolitan Governor of Hezhong, and military commissioner of Hezhong-Jin-Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was dismissed from the chancellorship and made Acting Minister of Works, Associate Councilor of State, Metropolitan Governor of Hezhong, and military commissioner of Hezhong-Jin-Jiang.

sentences.zh: 咸通二年，改汴州刺史、宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantong he was changed to prefect of Bian and military commissioner of Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiantong he was changed to prefect of Bian and military commissioner of Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，遷揚州大都督府長史、淮南節度副大使、知節度事。

translations.literal: In winter of the third year he was transferred to Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Prefecture of Yang, Vice Military Commissioner of Huainan, and acting military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the third year he was transferred to Chief Administrator of the Metropolitan Prefecture of Yang, Vice Military Commissioner of Huainan, and acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累加開府儀同三司、檢校司徒，進食邑至三千戶。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to Grand Master of Honor with the Golden Tally and Acting Minister of Works, and his fief was increased to three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly advanced to Grand Master of Honor with the Golden Tally and Acting Minister of Works, and his fief was increased to three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 九年，徐州戍兵龐勛自桂州擅還。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Xu Prefecture garrison troops under Pang Xun returned without authorization from Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Xu Prefecture garrison troops under Pang Xun returned without authorization from Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七月至浙西，沿江自白沙入濁河，剽奪舟船而進。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they reached Zhexi, entered the muddy river from Baisha along the river, plundered boats and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they reached Zhexi, entered the muddy river from Baisha along the river, plundered boats and advanced.

sentences.zh: 綯聞勛至，遣使慰撫，供給芻米。

translations.literal: When Tao heard Xun had arrived he sent envoys to comfort and supply fodder and rice.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao heard Xun had arrived he sent envoys to comfort and supply fodder and rice.

sentences.zh: 都押衙李湘白綯曰：「徐兵擅還，必無好意。

translations.literal: Chief Military Escort Li Xiang told Tao: "The Xu troops returned without authorization—they surely have no good intent.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Military Escort Li Xiang told Tao: "The Xu troops returned without authorization—they surely have no good intent.

sentences.zh: 雖無詔命除討，權變制在籓方。

translations.literal: Though there is no edict ordering suppression, expedient authority to act lies with the frontier governor.
translations.idiomatic: Though there is no edict ordering suppression, expedient authority to act lies with the frontier governor.

sentences.zh: 昨其黨來投，言其數不逾二千，而虛張舟航旗幟，恐人見其實。

translations.literal: Yesterday their party came to surrender and said their number did not exceed two thousand, yet they falsely displayed boats, banners, and flags, fearing people would see their true strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday their party came to surrender and said their number did not exceed two thousand, yet they falsely displayed boats, banners, and flags, fearing people would see their true strength.

sentences.zh: 涉境已來，心頗憂惴。

translations.literal: Since they crossed the border I have been quite anxious.
translations.idiomatic: Since they crossed the border I have been quite anxious.

sentences.zh: 計其水路，須出高郵縣界，河岸鬥峻而水深狹。

translations.literal: Considering their water route, they must pass the border of Gaoyou County; the river bank is steep and the water deep and narrow.
translations.idiomatic: Considering their water route, they must pass the border of Gaoyou County, where the river bank is steep and the water deep and narrow.

sentences.zh: 若出奇兵邀之，俾荻船縱火於前，勁兵奮擊於後，敗走必矣。

translations.literal: If surprise troops are sent to intercept them, set fire to reed boats ahead and strike fiercely from behind, they will surely flee in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: If surprise troops are sent to intercept them, set fire to reed boats ahead and strike fiercely from behind, they will surely flee in defeat.

sentences.zh: 若不於此誅鋤，俟濟淮、泗，合徐人負怨之徒，不下十萬，則禍亂非細也。」

translations.literal: If they are not destroyed here, when they cross the Huai and Si and join Xu people bearing grievances, they will number no less than one hundred thousand—then calamity and disorder will be no small matter."
translations.idiomatic: If they are not destroyed here, when they cross the Huai and Si and join Xu people bearing grievances, they will number no less than one hundred thousand—then calamity and disorder will be no small matter."

sentences.zh: 綯性懦緩，又以不奉詔命，謂湘曰：「長淮已南，他不為暴。

translations.literal: Tao was by nature timid and slow, and because he had no imperial edict he told Xiang: "South of the Long Huai they will not commit violence.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was by nature timid and slow, and because he had no imperial edict he told Xiang: "South of the Long Huai they will not commit violence.

sentences.zh: 從他過去，余非吾事也。」

translations.literal: Let them pass by—the rest is not my affair."
translations.idiomatic: Let them pass by—the rest is not my affair."

sentences.zh: 其年冬，龐勛殺崔彥曾，據徐州，聚眾六七萬。

translations.literal: That winter Pang Xun killed Cui Yanzeng, seized Xu Prefecture, and gathered a host of sixty or seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Pang Xun killed Cui Yanzeng, seized Xu Prefecture, and gathered a host of sixty or seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 徐無兵食，乃分遣賊帥攻剽淮南諸郡，滁、和、楚、壽繼陷。

translations.literal: Xu had no troops or grain, so they sent bandit chiefs to raid the prefectures of Huainan; Chu, He, Chu, and Shou fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Xu had no troops or grain, so they sent bandit chiefs to raid the prefectures of Huainan. Chu, He, Chu, and Shou fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 谷食既盡，淮南之民多為賊所啖。

translations.literal: When grain was exhausted, many people of Huainan were eaten by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When grain was exhausted, many people of Huainan were eaten by the bandits.

sentences.zh: 時兩淮郡縣多陷，唯杜慆守泗州，賊攻之經年，不能下。

translations.literal: At that time many prefectures and counties of the two Huai regions had fallen; only Du Tao held Si Prefecture, and though the bandits attacked for a year they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many prefectures and counties of the two Huai regions had fallen. Only Du Tao held Si Prefecture, and though the bandits attacked for a year they could not take it.

sentences.zh: 初，詔綯為徐州南面招討使。

translations.literal: Initially an edict appointed Tao Pacification Commissioner south of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Initially an edict appointed Tao Pacification Commissioner south of Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賊攻泗州急，綯令李湘將兵五千人援之。

translations.literal: When the bandits pressed the attack on Si Prefecture, Tao ordered Li Xiang to lead five thousand troops to aid it.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits pressed the attack on Si Prefecture, Tao ordered Li Xiang to lead five thousand troops to aid it.

sentences.zh: 賊聞湘來援，遣人致書於綯，辭情遜順，言：「朝廷累有詔赦宥，但抗拒者三兩人耳，旦夕圖去之，即束身請命，願相公保任之。」

translations.literal: When the bandits heard Xiang was coming to aid, they sent a man with a letter to Tao, humble and compliant in tone, saying: "The court has repeatedly issued edicts of pardon; only two or three men resist. We plan to remove them before long, then bind ourselves and beg for orders—we hope the Lord Chancellor will vouch for us."
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits heard Xiang was coming to aid, they sent a man with a letter to Tao, humble and compliant in tone, saying: "The court has repeatedly issued edicts of pardon. Only two or three men resist. We plan to remove them before long, then bind ourselves and beg for orders—we hope the Lord Chancellor will vouch for us."

sentences.zh: 綯即奏聞，請賜勛節鉞，仍誡李湘但戍淮口，賊已招降，不得立異。

translations.literal: Tao immediately reported to the throne and requested that Xun be granted the staff of command, and also warned Li Xiang only to garrison the Huai mouth—the bandits had already surrendered and he must not act differently.
translations.idiomatic: Tao immediately reported to the throne and requested that Xun be granted the staff of command. He also warned Li Xiang only to garrison the Huai mouth—the bandits had already surrendered and he must not act differently.

sentences.zh: 由是湘軍解甲安寢，去警徹備，日與賊軍相對，歡笑交言。

translations.literal: Because of this Xiang's army laid aside armor and slept peacefully, relaxed vigilance and defenses, and daily faced the bandit army laughing and conversing.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this Xiang's army laid aside armor and slept peacefully, relaxed vigilance and defenses, and daily faced the bandit army laughing and conversing.

sentences.zh: 一日，賊軍乘間，步騎徑入湘壘，淮卒五千人皆被生縶送徐州，為賊蒸而食之。

translations.literal: One day the bandit army seized an opening; infantry and cavalry entered Xiang's camp directly, and all five thousand Huai soldiers were captured alive and sent to Xu Prefecture to be steamed and eaten by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: One day the bandit army seized an opening. Infantry and cavalry entered Xiang's camp directly, and all five thousand Huai soldiers were captured alive and sent to Xu Prefecture to be steamed and eaten by the bandits.

sentences.zh: 湘與監軍郭厚本為龐勛斷手足，以徇於康承訓軍。

translations.literal: Xiang and Military Commissioner Guo Houben had their hands and feet cut off by Pang Xun and were displayed before Kang Chengxun's army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang and Military Commissioner Guo Houben had their hands and feet cut off by Pang Xun and were displayed before Kang Chengxun's army.

sentences.zh: 時浙西杜審權發軍千人，與李湘約會兵，大將翟行約勇敢知名。

translations.literal: At that time Zhexi's Du Shenquan sent one thousand troops to join Xiang in combined operations; the great general Zhai Xingyue was brave and famous.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhexi's Du Shenquan sent one thousand troops to join Xiang in combined operations. The great general Zhai Xingyue was brave and famous.

sentences.zh: 浙軍未至而湘軍敗。

translations.literal: The Zhe army had not yet arrived when Xiang's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhe army had not yet arrived when Xiang's army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 賊乃分兵，立淮南旗幟，為交鬥之狀。

translations.literal: The bandits then divided their forces, raised Huainan banners, and made a show of mutual combat.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then divided their forces, raised Huainan banners, and made a show of mutual combat.

sentences.zh: 行約軍望見，急趨之，千人並為賊所縛。

translations.literal: Xingyue's army saw them and hurried toward them; all one thousand were bound by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyue's army saw them and hurried toward them. All one thousand were bound by the bandits.

sentences.zh: 送徐州。

translations.literal: They were sent to Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: They were sent to Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 綯既喪師，朝廷以左衛大將軍、徐州西南面招討使馬舉代綯為淮南節度使。

translations.literal: Since Tao had lost his army, the court sent Left Guard General Ma Ju, Southwest Pacification Commissioner for Xu Prefecture, to replace Tao as military commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tao had lost his army, the court sent Left Guard General Ma Ju, Southwest Pacification Commissioner for Xu Prefecture, to replace Tao as military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 十二年八月，授檢校司徒、太子太保，分司東都。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year he was appointed Acting Minister of Works and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, assigned to the Eastern Capital as titular official.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twelfth year he was appointed Acting Minister of Works and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, assigned to the Eastern Capital as titular official.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以本官為鳳翔尹、鳳翔隴節度使，進封趙國公，食邑三千戶，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, with his regular office he became Metropolitan Governor of Fengxiang and military commissioner of Fengxiang-Long, advanced to Duke of Zhao with a fief of three thousand households, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, with his regular office he became Metropolitan Governor of Fengxiang and military commissioner of Fengxiang-Long, advanced to Duke of Zhao with a fief of three thousand households, and died.

sentences.zh: 子滈、渙、沨。

translations.literal: His sons Hao, Huan, and Fen.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Hao, Huan, and Fen.

sentences.zh: 滈，少舉進士，以父在內職而止。

translations.literal: Hao, while young, took the jinshi examination but stopped because his father held an inner-court post.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, while young, took the jinshi examination but stopped because his father held an inner-court post.

sentences.zh: 及綯輔政十年，滈以鄭顥之親，驕縱不法，日事遊宴，貨賄盈門，中外為之側目。

translations.literal: When Tao assisted in government for ten years, Hao, through kinship with Zheng Hao, was arrogant and lawless, daily given to feasting and pleasure, and bribes filled his gate; inside and outside all watched him sidelong.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao assisted in government for ten years, Hao, through kinship with Zheng Hao, was arrogant and lawless, daily given to feasting and pleasure, and bribes filled his gate. Inside and outside all watched him sidelong.

sentences.zh: 以綯黨援方盛，無敢措言。

translations.literal: Because Tao's factional support was then flourishing, none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tao's factional support was then flourishing, none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 及懿宗即位，訟者不一，故綯罷權軸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yizong acceded, complainants were not few, and so Tao was dismissed from the axis of power.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yizong acceded, complainants were not few, and so Tao was dismissed from the axis of power.

sentences.zh: 既至河中，上言曰：「臣男滈，爰自孩提，便從師訓，至於詞藝，頗及輩流。

translations.literal: After reaching Hezhong he submitted a memorial saying: "My son Hao, from infancy followed teachers' instruction; in literary skill he compares well with his peers.
translations.idiomatic: After reaching Hezhong he submitted a memorial saying: "My son Hao, from infancy followed teachers' instruction. In literary skill he compares well with his peers.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年，臣任戶部員外郎時，已令應舉，至大中二年猶未成名。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huichang, when I was Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, I already had him take the examination; by the second year of Dazhong he still had not achieved fame.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huichang, when I was Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, I already had him take the examination. By the second year of Dazhong he still had not achieved fame.

sentences.zh: 臣自湖州刺史蒙先帝擢授考功郎中、知制誥，尋充學士。

translations.literal: I, from prefect of Hu Prefecture, received the late emperor's promotion to Director in the Bureau of Evaluations and Drafter of Imperial Edicts, and soon became Academician.
translations.idiomatic: I, from prefect of Hu Prefecture, received the late emperor's promotion to Director in the Bureau of Evaluations and Drafter of Imperial Edicts, and soon became Academician.

sentences.zh: 繼叨渥澤，遂忝樞衡，事體有妨，因令罷舉，自當廢絕，一十九年。

translations.literal: Then receiving generous favor I disgraced the pivot of power; the matter was improper, so I ordered him to stop the examination and it should have ended—nineteen years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Then receiving generous favor I disgraced the pivot of power. The matter was improper, so I ordered him to stop the examination and it should have ended—nineteen years in all.

sentences.zh: 每遣退藏，更令勤勵。

translations.literal: Each time I was sent to withdraw, yet again urged to diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I was sent to withdraw, yet again urged to diligence.

sentences.zh: 臣以祿位逾分，齒發已衰。

translations.literal: My rank and salary exceed my due; my teeth and hair are already declining.
translations.idiomatic: My rank and salary exceed my due; my teeth and hair are already declining.

sentences.zh: 男滈年過長成，未沾一第，犬馬私愛，實切憫傷。

translations.literal: My son Hao has passed grown age without winning a degree; paternal affection deeply pains me.
translations.idiomatic: My son Hao has passed grown age without winning a degree; paternal affection deeply pains me.

sentences.zh: 臣二三年來，頻乞罷免，每年取得文解，意待才離中書，便令赴舉。

translations.literal: For two or three years I have repeatedly begged dismissal; each year I obtained examination credentials, intending once I left the Secretariat to have him take the examination.
translations.idiomatic: For two or three years I have repeatedly begged dismissal. Each year I obtained examination credentials, intending once I left the Secretariat to have him take the examination.

sentences.zh: 昨蒙恩制，寵以近籓。

translations.literal: Yesterday I received an imperial edict favoring him with a nearby frontier post.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I received an imperial edict favoring him with a nearby frontier post.

sentences.zh: 伏緣已逼禮部試期，便令就試。

translations.literal: Because the Ministry of Rites examination period was already near, I had him take the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Ministry of Rites examination period was already near, I had him take the examination.

sentences.zh: 至於與奪，出自主司，臣固不敢撓其衡柄。

translations.literal: As for success or failure, it lies with the chief examiner; I truly dare not interfere with his balance.
translations.idiomatic: As for success or failure, it lies with the chief examiner. I truly dare not interfere with his balance.

sentences.zh: 臣初離機務，合具上聞。

translations.literal: When I first left the pivot of power I ought to have reported fully to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When I first left the pivot of power I ought to have reported fully to the throne.

sentences.zh: 昨延英奉辭，本擬面奏，伏以戀恩方切，陳誠至難。

translations.literal: Yesterday at an Yanying audience to take leave I originally intended to report face to face, but considering my longing for favor was then keen, to state my sincerity was extremely hard.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday at an Yanying audience to take leave I originally intended to report face to face, but considering my longing for favor was then keen, to state my sincerity was extremely hard.

sentences.zh: 伏冀宸慈，察臣丹懇。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope for imperial kindness to discern my earnest sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope for imperial kindness to discern my earnest sincerity."

sentences.zh: 詔令就試。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to take the examination.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to take the examination.

sentences.zh: 是歲，中書舍人裴坦權知貢舉，登第者三十人。

translations.literal: That year Palace Secretary Pei Tan acted as chief examiner; thirty passed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Palace Secretary Pei Tan acted as chief examiner; thirty passed.

sentences.zh: 有鄭羲者，故戶部尚書浣之孫，裴弘余，故相休之子，魏綯故相扶之子，及滈，皆名臣子第，言無實才。

translations.literal: Among them were Zheng Yi, grandson of former Minister of Revenue Huan; Pei Hongyu, son of former Chancellor Xiu; Wei Tao, son of former Chancellor Fu; and Hao—all sons of famed ministers, said to lack real talent.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were Zheng Yi, grandson of former Minister of Revenue Huan; Pei Hongyu, son of former Chancellor Xiu; Wei Tao, son of former Chancellor Fu; and Hao—all sons of famed ministers, said to lack real talent.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫崔瑄上疏論之曰：「令狐滈昨以父居相位，權在一門。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Cui Xuan submitted a memorial criticizing this, saying: "Linghu Hao yesterday, because his father held the chancellorship, had power in one gate.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Cui Xuan submitted a memorial criticizing this, saying: "Linghu Hao yesterday, because his father held the chancellorship, had power in one gate.

sentences.zh: 求請者詭黨風趨，妄動者群邪雲集。

translations.literal: Those who sought favors flocked like wind to a clique; those who acted rashly gathered like clouds of the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sought favors flocked like wind to a clique; those who acted rashly gathered like clouds of the wicked.

sentences.zh: 每歲貢闈登第，在朝清列除官，事望雖出於綯，取舍全由於滈。

translations.literal: Each year when candidates passed the examination gate and the pure ranks of court received office, though the matter seemed to come from Tao, selection lay entirely with Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Each year when candidates passed the examination gate and the pure ranks of court received office, though the matter seemed to come from Tao, selection lay entirely with Hao.

sentences.zh: 喧然如市，旁若無人，權動寰中，勢傾天下。

translations.literal: The clamor was like a market, as if no one else existed; his power moved within the realm and his momentum overturned the world.
translations.idiomatic: The clamor was like a market, as if no one else existed. His power moved within the realm and his momentum overturned the world.

sentences.zh: 及綯罷相作鎮之日，便令滈納卷貢闈。

translations.literal: On the day Tao left the chancellorship to govern a frontier post he had Hao submit his examination papers.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Tao left the chancellorship to govern a frontier post he had Hao submit his examination papers.

sentences.zh: 豈可以父在樞衡，獨撓文柄？

translations.literal: How can the father be at the pivot of power yet alone twist the literary handle?
translations.idiomatic: How can the father be at the pivot of power yet alone twist the literary handle?

sentences.zh: 請下御史臺按問文解日月者。」

translations.literal: I beg that the Censorate be ordered to investigate according to the dates of the examination papers."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Censorate be ordered to investigate according to the dates of the examination papers."

sentences.zh: 奏疏不下。

translations.literal: The memorial was not issued.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was not issued.

sentences.zh: 滈既及第，釋褐長安尉、集賢校理。

translations.literal: After Hao passed he left office as warden of Chang'an and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao passed he left office as warden of Chang'an and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 咸通二年，遷右拾遺、史館修撰。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantong he was promoted to Right Reminder and Compiler of the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiantong he was promoted to Right Reminder and Compiler of the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 制出，左拾遺劉蛻、起居郎張雲，各上疏極論滈云：「恃父秉權，恣受貨賂。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Left Reminder Liu Tui and Attendant of the Left Liu Yun each submitted memorials strongly criticizing Hao, saying: "Relying on his father's wielding of power, he freely accepted bribes.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Left Reminder Liu Tui and Attendant of the Left Liu Yun each submitted memorials strongly criticizing Hao, saying: "Relying on his father's wielding of power, he freely accepted bribes.

sentences.zh: 取李琢錢，除琢安南都護，遂致蠻陷交州。」

translations.literal: He took money from Li Zhuo and had Zhuo appointed Protector-General of Annan, thus causing the barbarians to seize Jiaozhou."
translations.idiomatic: He took money from Li Zhuo and had Zhuo appointed Protector-General of Annan, thus causing the barbarians to seize Jiaozhou."

sentences.zh: 張雲言：「大中十年，襜以諫議大夫豆盧籍、刑部郎中李鄴為夔王已下侍讀，欲立夔王為東宮，欲亂先朝子弟之序。

translations.literal: Liu Yun said: "In the tenth year of Dazhong, Can had Remonstrance Official Dou Luji and Director in the Ministry of Justice Li Ye serve as tutors to the Prince of Kui and those below, wishing to establish the Prince of Kui as Heir Apparent and disturb the order of the late emperor's sons.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun said: "In the tenth year of Dazhong, Can had Remonstrance Official Dou Luji and Director in the Ministry of Justice Li Ye serve as tutors to the Prince of Kui and those below, wishing to establish the Prince of Kui as Heir Apparent and disturb the order of the late emperor's sons.

sentences.zh: 滈內倚鄭顥，人誰敢言？」

translations.literal: Hao inwardly relied on Zheng Hao—who dared speak?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao inwardly relied on Zheng Hao—who dared speak?"

sentences.zh: 時襜在淮南，累表自雪。

translations.literal: At that time Can was in Huainan and repeatedly submitted memorials to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Can was in Huainan and repeatedly submitted memorials to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 懿宗重傷大臣意，貶雲為興元少尹，蛻為華陰令，改滈詹事府司直。

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong deeply hurt the feelings of great ministers; Yun was demoted to Vice Governor of Xingyuan, Tui to magistrate of Huayin, and Hao was changed to Direct Clerk of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong deeply hurt the feelings of great ministers. Yun was demoted to Vice Governor of Xingyuan, Tui to magistrate of Huayin, and Hao was changed to Direct Clerk of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 滈為眾所非，宦名不達。

translations.literal: Hao was condemned by all and his official reputation did not prosper.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was condemned by all and his official reputation did not prosper.

sentences.zh: 渙、沨俱登進士第。

translations.literal: Huan and Fen both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Huan and Fen both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 渙位至中書舍人。

translations.literal: Huan reached Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Huan reached Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 定子緘，緘子澄、湘。

translations.literal: Ding's son Jian; Jian's sons Cheng and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ding's son Jian; Jian's sons Cheng and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 澄亦以進士登第，累辟使府。

translations.literal: Cheng also passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly recruited to commissioner staffs.
